questions.question: When getting ready to change lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Then quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for oncoming vehicles or pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from the left will be closer to you than those from the right. Check across the entire intersection before you move.

questions.question: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Keep moving and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue moving and clear the intersection safely.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and request an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need longer distances to stop and speed up than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas you cannot see when you are tired.
Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Check the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called 'blind spots' because you cannot see them in your mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
A right turn is allowed only on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs have a fluorescent yellow-green background. These signs warn you about upcoming road conditions, such as curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what lights should you use so others can see you?
questions.explanation: When daylight begins to fade, turn on your low beam headlights so others can see you. Only use high beam headlights in open areas with no other drivers nearby.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: It is important to check traffic behind you when:
questions.explanation: Check traffic behind you at least every 10 seconds. This is especially important when changing lanes, backing up, slowing down, or driving down steep hills.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Your braking distance depends on three things: how fast you are driving, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You must change how you drive when the weather changes suddenly.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When the weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Pay attention to vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What is a major cause of deadly and serious crash injuries?

options.text: Driving with more than one child in the car.
Driving while under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Taking frequent rest stops on long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving while under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or other drugs. In Nebraska, this is a major cause of deadly and serious crash injuries.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?

options.text: One driver who continues without stopping.
One driver who waves the others ahead.

questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who reached the intersection first has the right to go first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: When should you let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if they wave at you first.
Only if they are not texting while walking.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian cross. You may proceed carefully only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go ahead since you have the right-of-way.
Go ahead if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must give the right-of-way to anyone in the intersection. If a pedestrian started crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal began, wait until they have completely crossed before you go.

questions.question: When you see a disabled person with a guide dog, white cane, or other device, you should yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A pedestrian with a disability using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other device has the right-of-way, whether on a sidewalk or roadway. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows a law drivers must follow. Right turns are not permitted at this location.

questions.question: Should you be careful when passing large vehicles and avoid driving next to them for long periods?
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Avoid staying next to a large vehicle for a long time. It is safer to either drop back or move ahead.

questions.question: How can you make sure your physical condition does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay in good physical shape and have regular checkups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. Know your physical limits and only drive if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This rule applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to stop for a red light or slow for a yellow light.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance work areas?
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive with extra caution when you see orange warning devices on the road.

questions.question: Before turning right at a red traffic light, what should a driver do?

options.text: Slow down and go if the way is clear.
Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
Keep going at the same speed because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot. Always come to a complete stop first. Look both ways and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must a driver show?
questions.explanation: Drivers must carry and show three documents when stopped: a driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You need all three documents in your vehicle when driving.
